title: Technicals Support New Highs for Nasdaq 100, BofA Merrill's Suttmeier Says
description: Jul.24 -- On this edition of "Charting Futures," Steve Suttmeier, Bank of America Merrill Lynch technical analyst, examines the performance of tech and growth stocks with Bloomberg's Abigail Doolittle on "Bloomberg Markets: The Close."

asr.full_text: Tech is the top sector on the year up in a big way of about 30 percent and a big piece of that, the fang trade, although that's also the communication services. Today, you see the fang trade is really drifting around with Facebook, Amazon, Netflix and Alphabet mixed trading action. Facebook, though, reversing a big loss earlier, of course, in the news that they will, in fact, be paying that five billion dollar fine, a record fine to the FTC on antitrust and privacy issues. They of course report tonight after the bell and a year ago they put up the worst quarter ever that stock at that point plunging 20 percent but investors looking for a little bit more. In fact they're looking for 25 percent growth for revenues. Amazon and Alphabet they report tomorrow and Netflix of course they put up a weak quarter last week and that could be what's weighing overall in the FANG trade. When we go into the Bloomberg let's take a look at this longer term chart. Out of 2016 we see a beautiful uptrend where the bulls, the buyers very much in control, a solid MACD buy signal and then come 2018 as the fears around the idea that regulation could come to big tech, we see these huge waves of uncertainty, a piece of that of course around Facebook and their data scandal. Right now, the FANG trade, and this is the true Facebook, Amazon, Netflix, and Alphabet coming back down into a range. The MACD appears to be on a sell signal, so it may suggest that there could be some wishy-washy trading, maybe even some bearish trading ahead. So I'd like to talk to Steve Suttmeier of Bank of America, Merrill Lynch, a little bit about this. And what do you think of that chart? Does that worry you at all in terms of tech or the FANG trade? Well, I mean, to me it looks like a consolidation and a larger uptrend. Sure, it can pull back a little bit further here, but I see a lot of stock charts that have that set up, where you rally back to the highs, pull back a bit. It wouldn't take much to get that to break out. So that's what I'm paying attention to in the longer-term uptrend. And so let's take a look at your chart of the NASDAQ 100 futures, because something that people don't realize, this is a nice proxy for the FANG trade, even though the charts are a little bit different, but 25% weighting. And your trading idea here, in fact, supports the idea that you're a little bit cautious, but you're mainly bullish. Exactly. So thanks, Abigail. So when you look at this particular chart, what you see here is a a longer term rising trend for the NASDAQ 100 e-mini futures and what we like about the chart is it's holding trend at the moment. It's above a 21 day moving average and that act has support around 78.15. You also have this projected rising channel. So what we're doing here is we're buying any dips above the 78.15. There's also a little bit of support around 7855 and we think if that level holds we break out to new highs and move towards this 8200 range so roughly 8185 to 8250 so that's what we think can happen and we have our stop loss below that that we're calling it below 7800 but that means you would break that last higher low I remember if we start breaking the 21 day moving average that could mean that you follow You have a very thin price chart here, though, and one of the strategies here is to go into the high 40s and stay low for the upper 40s rather than that kind of low at the point that it takes for a buyback of your trade to close for a very long period. So you could be breaking the 21-day move, but it could mean that you're still a negative seasonality that comes in in August. Yeah, so that stop certainly protects you from any possible weakness on the FANG trade. But supporting your bullish view here on the NASDAQ 100 futures, if you could talk to us about this quickly. Sure, definitely. whether growth is going to be valued. At this point growth is still leadership versus value. We view the current pattern as a break out and re-test for Russ 1000 growth versus Russ 1000 value. And the same thing happened in 2017. A lot of people are saying there's a negative divergence on the RSI. There's a 14 week RSI. But as long as we hold that support range, roughly around 60 to 59 on the 14 week RSI, I think growth continues to grind higher versus value.
